City Civil & Sessions Judge, Commercial Court, Bengaluru (Cch-83) Present: Sri. Vidyadhar Shirahatti, Ll.M., Lxxxii Addl. City Civil & Sessions Judge, Bengaluru. Com.O.S.No.1179/2023 Dated on this 17th Day of November 2025 Plaintiff 1. Mrs. Lizy Varghese, Wife of George Varghese. P, aged about 65 years, Residing at No. 4, Priya Villa, 4th block, , Hbr Layour, Kalyan Nagar Post, Bangalore - 560 043. 2. Mr. George Varghese. P, Son of K.C. texts.facts: The suit filed by the plaintiff for seeking an order directing the Defendants to quit and deliver the vacant possession of the Schedule Property forthwith, failing COM.O.S.1179/2023 which the Plaintiffs be at liberty to secure the vacant possession of Schedule Property through the process of this court at the cost of the Defendants. (ii) Directing the Defendant to pay to the Plaintiffs a sum of Rs. 6,55,000/- being the arrears of rent together with current and future interest thereon @ 24% per annum to be computed from the date of institution of suit till the date of payment and that amount be payable from all the Defendants jointly, severally and personally. (iii) Directing the Defendant for damages to effect payment of a sum of Rs. 2,00,000/- per month or part thereof to the Plaintiffs for the use and occupation of the Schedule Property post the termination of tenancy as "tenants of sufferance" from the date of institution of this suit till the delivery of vacant possession. (v) To pass an order for an enquiry for payment of additional mense profits to be computed in an appropriate Final Decree Proceedings in terms of Order COM.O.S.1179/2023 XX Rule 12 if the CPC to be computed from the date of termination of the tenancy till the date of delivery of possession of the Schedule Property in excess of Rs. 2,00,000/- per month or part thereof; 2. The Brief facts as per Plaint are as follows:- 2.1. The schedule property is the subject matter of lease by the Plaintiff in favour of the Defendant No. 1 a Partnership Firm of which the Defendants 2 and 3 are the Partners. The Schedule Property is a commercial property and was leased to the Defendants for commercial purpose to carry on the business of a Restaurant in the name and style of "Khayal". The present rate of rent payable per month is Rs.1,25,000/. The area of the Schedule Property is in excess of 14 Square Meters and is in extent of 2580 Square feet. The Deed of Lease executed by the Plaintiffs in favour of the Defendants is in the custody of the Defendants. The Schedule Property is being used for commercial purposes and was let out to the Defendants for the purpose of carrying out commercial activity exclusively. COM.O.S.1179/2023 2.2. The Defendants are tenants of the Schedule Property on a month to month basis. The Defendants No. 1 to 3 are running a restaurant under the name and style of 'Khayal Lizy Varghese vs M/S Khorshid Hospitality And Corporate ... on 17 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49479964/ 3 Restaurant'. The Defendant No. 1 of which Defendants No. 2 and 3 are the Partners are chronic defaulters of payment of rent. As of the end of August 2023, the Defendants are due a sum of Rs.6,55,000/-. In spite of repeated requests and reminders, the Defendants have not shown any interest in demonstrating the intention to pay the arrears of rent as against a total due of Rs.22,45,000/-. The Defendants have paid a sum of Rs.15,90,000/-. The rent payable is excluding the GST applicable. In these circumstances and on account of repeated default in payment of arrears of rent and on account of GST, the Plaintiffs were constrained to issue a notice to the Defendants through their Counsel dated 26.08.2023. The notice to the Defendants was sent to the office of the Partnership Firm and to the Schedule Property. The notice to the firm was returned with a Postal Endorsement, "No such office in this address, hence returned to the Sender". The notice sent to the Schedule Property was attempted for service by way of COM.O.S.1179/2023 an intimation delivered on 29.08.2023 and 30.08.2023 by the postman. In spite of intimation, the said notices were unclaimed and therefore the notice was returned with a postal endorsement dated 08.09.2023 to the effect "Unclaimed". 2.3. The Plaintiffs on account of the return of the notice dated 26.08.2023, ascertained the residential address of the Defendants No. 2 and 3 and reissued the notice containing the same date that is 26.08.2023 and dispatched the said notice to the Defendants No. 2 and 3 on 15.09.2023, which residential address is also reflected in the cause title to the present suit. The postal receipts of the notice sent to the said address. The said notice was served to the Defendants No. 2 and 3 on 18.09.2023. The track consignment report as maintained by India Post, Department of Post, Government of India. The Defendants upon receipt of the notice addressed to their residence have caused a reply through their Counsel dated 05.10.2023. The Defendants in the reply have refused to comply with the lawful demand of the Plaintiffs to quit and deliver vacant possession of the Schedule Property whilst COM.O.S.1179/2023 admitting that they are tenants of the Schedule Property, and hence the present suit. 3. After service of summons, the Defendant has appeared and filed written statement and contention that, the schedule property was subject to lease in favour of Defendants for the purpose of running a Food and Beverage restaurant under the style and name of Khayal Restaurant. The monthly rent for the restaurant starting from the commencement of lease period i.e., 01.04.2022 is Rs. 90,000/- per month including the GST. The deed of lease executed by the plaintiff in favour of the defendant is is the custody of the Defendant. The suit schedule property leased to the Defendants on a month to month are grossly wrong and misleading. The lease for the schedule property is a long term lease of 6 years and further to extension after expiry of the 6 years lease term. The plaintiffs must be put to strict proof and asked to disclose the facts and to prove and submit all necessary documents. 3.1. The Defendants have made a payment of Rs. 11,50,000/- towards the rentals as of the date made COM.O.S.1179/2023 through cheques and online bank transfers. In addition, the earlier monthly rental amounts paid to the Plaintiff amount to Rs. 15,90,000/-. The Defendants have also paid an amount of Rs.6,00,000/- as Security Deposit, which is with the Plaintiff in the entire amount. The Defendants have incurred substantial expenses and made payments, on behalf of the Plaintiff in the entire amount. The legal Notice was sent to the office of the partnership firm of the Defendants and it was returned with a postal endorsement "No such office in this address". 5. To prove its case, the plaintiff has examined Narayan Lal as a PW1 and relied 4 documents marked as Exhibit P1 to P4. The plaintiff has taken a contention that the Defendant is due of Rs. 6,55,000/- rent and is liable to pay interest at 24% per annum from the date of suit till its realization. It is also taken a contention that, the Defendant is liable to pay a Rs. 2,00,000/- per month for the use and occupation of the schedule property and posted the termination of tenancy. Therefore, the plaintiff filed this suit against the Defendant. However, the Defendant paid 90,000/- per month. Out of the said amount of Rs.5,90,000/- defendant paid. The plaintiff has issued a legal notice on dated 26.08.2023 where the notice was returned as no such office in this address, hence returned to the sender. The notice has been sent to the schedule property on 29.08.2023 and 30.08.2023 was returned as unclaimed. COM.O.S.1179/2023 10 . The plaintiff has mentioned about the recovery of Rs. 6,55,000/- with interest at 24% per annum in legal notice marked as Ex.P.1. the Postal receipts has been marked as Ex.P.2(a) to Ex.P.2(d). The plaintiff also issued a legal notice dated 26.08.2023 as per Ex.P.3 where in also the plaintiff has claimed Rs.6,55,000/- with interest at 24% per annum. However, after termination of legal notice, the plaintiff has claimed Rs. 2,00,000/- per month rent to the Suit schedule property. The postal receipts is marked as E.xP.3(a) and 3(b). The postal consignment have been submitted. 12. The Defendant has also issued a reply notice on dated 05.10.2023 wherein also denied the payment of Rs. 6,55,000/- as per the agreed rent. The Defendant has paid entire amount. There is no mark or seal. It is also admitted that, the rent was enhanced Rs. 1,25,000/- per month with effect from October 2022.
texts.arguments: The defendants have incurred substantial expenses and made Lizy Varghese vs M/S Khorshid Hospitality And Corporate ... on 17 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49479964/ 4 payments, on behalf of Plaintiffs, to confirm the schedule property to BESCOM'S regulatory requirements for rain harvesting and to carry out major electrical and sewage works to ensure safety and hygiene requirements of the schedule premises, which the Plaintiffs have neglected to carry out. Although the Defendants have made regular rental payments to the Plaintiffs, but the Plaintiffs have failed to give any rental invoices to the Defendants until now. Whenever, the Defendant demanded the rental invoice from plaintiff the plaintiff turned in to grave consequences. Therefore, the Plaintiffs allegation regarding the rental dues is misleading, baseless and not maintainable in law. The Defendants have also made several requests to meet the plaintiff to reconcile COM.O.S.1179/2023 the rental accounts and agree on the accurate rental accounts shown towards rental enhancements for Covid period, which were earlier verbally agreed by the Plaintiff to exempt or reduce the same. The Plaintiffs have deliberately ignored all such reduce the same. requests made by the Defendants. The plaintiffs had not made any such attempt. Hence he prayed to dismiss the suit. 9. To substantiate its contention Mr. Narayan Lal S/o R. Prabhakaran as a GPA holder examined as PW.1 and reiterated the plaint averments and relied 4 documents COM.O.S.1179/2023 marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.4. 13. In the cross-examination the Defendant has elicited from the mouth of the Plaintiff that, the GPA holder is father in law has executed the GPA to proceed with the case on behalf of both the plaintiffs. However, the DW.1 has stated in the cross-examination that the lease deed is not registered, the partnership firm is taken the property for lease to run the restaurant. He has received the termination notice marked as Ex.P.3 and 4. He has approached the City Civil court for filing the suit in O.S. No. 1519/2024 for injunction against the Plaintiff. It is admitted about the payment of rent of 9 months. The initial rent was fixed Rs. 90,000/- per month. 5% escalation is fixed for every 12 months. Lease commenced from October 2021. 3 months rent free period is October to December 2021.
